mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a term premium compression, reducing the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening episodes (t-test p > 0.05), or term premium expansion is observed instead.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a sustained demand surge, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS > 135000 in the prior two months
regime_hint: labor market tightening toward full employment
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60-day windows during such labor market episodes (t-test p > 0.05), or earnings revisions turn negative.

mechanism_narrative: A month-on-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding 2% signals accelerating business demand, which elevates optimism about future revenue and pushes up S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month growth > 2% in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite INDPRO acceleration (Rank IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for three consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which raises real discount rates and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or statistically indistinguishable from baseline during deflationary episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in residential housing starts turns positive for the first time in a contractionary cycle, it signals a bottoming in housing demand, reducing discounting of long-term equity prospects and producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month change > 0 for the first time in the prior contractionary quarter
failure_condition: No positive 60-day forward return occurs in such episodes, or housing starts continue contracting.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) above their prior month's levels indicates a labor market transition toward expansion, which increases investor confidence and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day return during such dual series moves (Rank IC < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the goods price index (RSAFS) below 50 for two consecutive months suggests persistent cost pressures, which compresses margins and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during such cost-pressure episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), the 6-month moving average of industrial production (GDPC1) growth exceeding 3% signals strong demand absorption, which elevates equity valuation multiples and yields positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return occurs when both triggers are met (Rank IC < -0.15).
